title: Functional in vitro and in vivo analysis of biosynthetic genes by heterologous expression in E. coli
protocol: Perform PCRs of the Gibson assembly fragments according to the protocol.
Calculate the correct extension time for the length of your fragment using Q5 polymerase (45 s per 1 kb for complex, GC-rich templates).
Run the PCR with the outlined cycling conditions.
Store the PCR reaction overnight at 4°C before agarose gel electrophoresis and DNA purification if necessary.
Perform agarose gel electrophoresis to check the PCR results.
Prepare a 1% agarose gel for the electrophoresis.
Place the gel tray in a gel caster to seal the edges of the gel tray.
Insert a comb with an appropriate number of wells into the comb guide of the gel tray.
Weigh 0.4 g agarose and suspend it in 40 mL 1× TAE buffer.
Heat the suspension to dissolve the agarose in a microwave.
Add 4 μL SYBR Safe after the agarose is completely dissolved.
Pour the gel solution into the gel tray and let it polymerize for approximately 20 minutes.
Prepare the electrophoresis chamber by filling it with 1× TAE buffer.
Place the polymerized gel into the electrophoresis chamber.
Take out 3 μL of 6× loading dye and divide it into two drops on parafilm (one drop per PCR sample).
Mix each PCR reaction sample (3 μL) with one of the loading dye drops on the parafilm.
Load the mixture into the wells of the gel starting from the second well.
Add 10 μL of DNA Ladder into the first well.
Run the gel for 30 minutes at 120 V.
Analyze the gel under UV light.
Add the calculated volume of DNA to the Gibson assembly master mix and adjust the volume to 20 μL with ddH2O.
Incubate the mixture for 1 h at 50°C in a thermocycler.
Remove the salts from the assembled plasmid.
Fill a Petri dish (Ø94 mm) approximately three quarters full with ultrapure water.
Place a MF-Millipore 0.025 μm MCE Membrane filter (13 mm) on the water surface using forceps and gloves to avoid touching it.
Carefully pipette the Gibson assembly mixture onto the filter and incubate it for 1 h with a closed lid.
After incubation, carefully transfer the Gibson assembly mixture into an Eppendorf tube.
Transform the assembled plasmid with E. coli Top10.
Thaw the competent cells on ice (skip this step if freshly prepared).
Add 5 μL of the salt-free Gibson assembly mix to the competent cells.
Transfer the mixture into an electroporation cuvette (0.2 cm gap) and ensure liquid is at the bottom without air bubbles.
Place the cuvette in an electroporator (MicroPulser; Bio-Rad) and apply a voltage of 2.5 kV (bacteria Ec2).
Immediately add 800 μL LB medium to the mixture, mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Transfer the culture into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube and incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
After incubation, centrifuge the culture for 4 min at 3000 × g.
Decant supernatant until only approximately 200 μL remains.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the remaining supernatant and spread it on an LB agarose plate containing kanamycin.
Incubate the agar plate overnight at 37°C.
Pick colonies from the incubated agar plate.
Plate picked colonies on a fresh LB agar plate containing kanamycin.
Use an autoclaved toothpick to pick up one colony, streak it in field number 1 and transfer the toothpick into the liquid medium of falcon tube number one.
Repeat this step with two more colonies using fields numbers 2 and 3 and corresponding tubes.
Incubate the agar plate at 37°C and the liquid cultures at 180 rpm and 37°C overnight.
Isolate plasmids from the bacterial cultures using a bacterial plasmid isolation kit.
Wrap the agar plate in parafilm for long-term storage at 4°C.
Perform a restriction digest with the three isolated plasmids.
Choose a restriction enzyme with cutting sites in your plasmid and the newly inserted fragment.
Measure the plasmid concentration with a NanoDrop.
Calculate the volume needed for 1000 ng of plasmid.
Prepare the restriction digest reaction mix by combining ingredients to be approximately 2.5 times larger than the plasmid volume.
Incubate the restriction digest mix according to the specific incubation temperature of the selected enzyme.
Add the appropriate amount of 6× loading dye to the reaction mix.
Load the whole reaction mix onto an agarose gel for electrophoresis.
Perform agarose gel electrophoresis as described in step 2.
Send the plasmid for sequencing if the correct restriction pattern appears on the gel.
Compare the sequence of the theoretical construct in SnapGene with the experimentally obtained sequence to verify the assembled plasmid.
Transform a mutation-free and correctly assembled plasmid with competent E. coli Bap1(DarR)/pGro7 cells as described, using kanamycin and chloramphenicol for selection.
Create glycerol stocks of the Top10 and Bap1 strains for long-term storage at −80°C.
Inoculate 4 mL LB medium supplemented with kanamycin with a colony from the stored E. coli Top10 plate that possesses the correct plasmid.
Likewise, inoculate 4 mL LB medium containing kanamycin and chloramphenicol with a colony of the E. coli Bap1/pGro7 strain created previously.
Incubate both cultures overnight at 37°C and 180 rpm in 15 mL falcon tubes.
Take 600 μL from each culture and add them to separate cryotubes containing 600 µL sterile 50% glycerol.
Carefully mix the contents of each tube by pipetting up and down.
Store the cryotubes at −80°C.
Inoculate 4 mL of LB medium supplemented with chloramphenicol and kanamycin with E. coli Bap1/pGro7/pJK6.1 in a 15 mL falcon tube.
Incubate the inoculated medium overnight at 37°C and 180 rpm.
Inoculate 20 mL of LB medium containing kanamycin and chloramphenicol with 1 mL of the overnight culture in a 100 mL flask.
Incubate the new culture at 37°C and 180 rpm until an OD600 value of 0.5 is reached.
Add IPTG to the culture as well as KBr.
Continue incubation for 3 days at 18°C and 180 rpm.
Take a sample from the culture after 3 days of incubation.
Prepare a 500 μL sample from the culture for centrifuging.
Centrifuge the 500 μL sample at 15,000 × g for 4 minutes.
Heat a hex wrench with a Bunsen burner.
Use the heated hex wrench to pierce a hole into the lid of a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Punch out two pieces (approximately 1 mm in diameter) of an Empore Octadecyl C18 47 mm extraction disk using a cannula.
Push the punched-out pieces of C18 sorbent into the tip of a pipette tip without packing it too tightly.
Equilibrate the column with 200 μL methanol by centrifugation at 3000 × g and 4°C for 4 minutes.
Remove the flowthrough after centrifugation.
Add 200 μL eluent 1 (5% acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid) to the column.
Centrifuge the column for 4 minutes at 3000 × g and 4°C.
Discard the flowthrough after centrifugation.
Add 200 μL of the sample supernatant to the column.
Centrifuge the column for 4 minutes at 3000 × g and 4°C.
Handle methanol carefully in a fume hood.
Pass the sample through the column completely within 4 minutes, increasing centrifugation time or speed if necessary.
Wash the column with 30 μL eluent 1 by centrifuging at 3000 × g and 4°C for 4 minutes.
Elute the column by adding 30 μL eluent 2 (20% acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid) and centrifuge for 4 minutes at 3000 × g and 4°C.
Repeat the elution step as necessary.
Transfer the sample to an LCMS vial.
Submit the sample to LCMS measurement.
Analyze the obtained data.
Inoculate 4 mL LB medium supplemented with chloramphenicol and kanamycin with E. coli Bap1/pGro7/pJK9.1 in a 15 mL falcon tube.
Incubate overnight at 37°C and 180 rpm.
The next day inoculate 100 mL LB medium containing kanamycin and chloramphenicol with 1 mL of the overnight culture in a 300 mL flask.
Incubate at 37°C and 180 rpm until an OD600 value of 0.5 is reached.
Induce the production by adding IPTG to the culture and continue incubation overnight at 18°C and 180 rpm.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation for 10 min at 10,000 × g and 4°C.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 4 mL cool QIAGEN lysis buffer.
Sonicate the cells for 35 seconds using settings cycle 7 and 70%.
Pause for 35 seconds.
Repeat sonication steps three times.
Pellet the cell debris by centrifugation at 4°C and 10,000 × g for 30 minutes.
Store the cleared supernatant at −20°C for up to 2 weeks.
Thaw the lysate on ice if frozen.
Add 5 μL of 4× NuPage LDS sample buffer to 20 μL of the cleared lysate and store at −20°C for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Purify the protein with a Ni-NTA column by adding 1 mL of Ni-NTA slurry into a polypropylene column.
Drain the storage liquid from the Ni-NTA column.
Add 4 mL of lysate to the Ni-NTA column and let it slowly elute.
Take a 20 μL sample from the flowthrough, add 5 μL of 4× NuPage LDS sample buffer, and store at −20°C for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Wash the column twice with 2.5 mL of QIAGEN wash buffer.
Collect washing fractions and mix 20 μL of each fraction with 5 μL of 4× NuPage LDS sample buffer.
Store the mixture at −20°C until used for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Elute the column four times with 0.5 mL QIAGEN elution buffer.
Take a sample of 20 μL from each elution fraction.
Add 5 μL of 4× NuPage LDS sample buffer to each sample.
Store the mixture at −20°C until SDS-PAGE analysis.
Store elution fractions with 10% glycerol.
Perform an SDS-PAGE analysis of the samples collected during purification.
Take a Mini-PROTEAN TGX Stain-Free gel from the package.
Remove the green tape from the bottom of the gel.
Assemble the Mini-PROTEAN tetra cell.
Add 1× running buffer into the inner and outer chamber.
Load the samples and 10 μL of PageRuler Prestained Protein Ladder into the wells of the gel.
Run the gel at 200 V until the dye reaches the bottom (approximately 30 minutes).
Open the gel cassette using the opening lever at the marked positions.
Stain the gel with ROTIBlue staining solution.
Mix 10 mL ROTIBlue, 30 mL ddH2O, and 10 mL methanol in a 50 mL flacon tube.
Incubate the gel shaking in the staining solution for 2 hours up to overnight.
If incubated overnight, destain the gel in water for 2 hours on the next day.
Use a camera to document the gel.
Prepare the halogenase in vitro assay mix according to the modified protocol by Zehner et al.
Incubate the assay mix at 18°C for 24 hours.
Add an equal amount of methanol to stop the reaction after incubation.
Centrifuge the mixture for 5 minutes at 15,000 × g.
Transfer the supernatant to a LCMS vial.
Subject the supernatant to LCMS measurement.
